Salad Days… You have my Heart ❤️!!

I recently tried the Falafel Pita Pocket, Greek Feta Pita Pocket, and the Broccoli Corn Pesto Sandwich— and each item was a delightful surprise.

The Pita Pockets were impressive - generously filled with fresh greens, olives, cucumbers, and crumbly feta. The flavors were vibrant, authentic  & perfectly spiced.

But the real standout was the Broccoli Corn Pesto Sandwich. It’s not something I expected to love as much as I did. The pesto was aromatic and rich, while the broccoli and corn added a nice texture and sweetness. It was hearty, fresh, and incredibly moreish.

The packaging was clean, eco-friendly, and kept everything intact without any mess.

Highly recommend Salad Days for anyone who values taste, quality, and freshness in every bite.

Please keep up the good work. Will definitely be ordering again soon!

featured_reviews.review_text: Enjoyed the food, loved the customer service and vibe and aesthetic. Peaceful and quiet place with good food but my highlight was the interaction with those working there❤️ Must visit

featured_reviews.name: Yash Rungta
featured_reviews.review_text:
A recent vegan lunch at Rare Earth Cafe turned out to be a genuinely delightful surprise.

Coming from a vegetarian family but someone who enjoys meat and seafood outside, I’ve always felt that the real advantage of being non-vegetarian is the freedom to eat anything—vegan, Jain, or otherwise. This place reinforces that idea beautifully.

Their cashew cheese is truly top-notch. It’s different from dairy cheese, but in a way that feels like an upgrade rather than a compromise. Everything tastes thoughtfully crafted. The flours they use—millets or emmer wheat—are light and easy to digest, which you can actually feel after the meal.

And the dessert? Easily a 7-star experience.

What stands out is their commitment to making everything in-house, using natural ingredients as much as possible. It shows in every bite.

You don’t need to be vegan to enjoy this place. Whether you’re vegetarian, non-vegetarian, eggetarian, Jain, or vegan—this café is absolutely worth a visit.

featured_reviews.name: V J
featured_reviews.review_text: A hidden culinary treasure tucked away in an unassuming building. Don’t be deceived by the exterior—the cuisine is exceptional, with every bite crafted with meticulous care and intention. This restaurant is essential for those with celiac disease or following a vegan diet. Begin your unforgettable gastronomic adventure with the sushi rolls, which serve as an excellent introduction to the menu. The proprietor is welcoming and has clearly procured premium ingredients. I’m confident this was my first experience tasting authentic wasabi.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

featured_reviews.review_text:
"I am a firm believer that how a cafe looks at 3:00 AM tells you everything you need to know about its quality. I stopped by late last night for a caffeine fix and was immediately struck by how clean and organized the space was—no messy counters or overflowing bins, just a pristine, welcoming atmosphere.
​I decided to try their pour-over, and I was impressed that the barista took the time to properly clean the equipment and rinse the filter before starting. The coffee was bright, clean, and perfectly extracted. It’s rare to find 24/7 service that doesn't compromise on hygiene or the 'slow coffee' experience. This is easily the best late-night spot in the city for anyone who values a premium brew in a well-maintained environment

featured_reviews.name: Rutuja Phirke
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters and really enjoyed the experience. The café has a calm, modern vibe that’s great for relaxing or working. The coffee is excellent, rich, flavorful, and clearly well crafted.

The food is decent and pairs well with the drinks, though coffee is definitely the highlight. Service is friendly.

Overall, a great spot for quality coffee.

featured_reviews.name: Abhijeet Devadiga
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely loved my experience at EarthBuns! This place is truly redefining what “healthy indulgence” means. We tried their burgers, wraps, warm salad bowls, and cold coffee, and every single item surprised us in the best way possible.

What stood out instantly is how clean yet flavor-packed everything tasted. Their gluten-free, zero-guilt burgers are honestly a game changer — no atta, no maida, no refined sugar, and yet the buns and patties were super satisfying. The air-fried plant-based patty and vegetable fries felt so light but still indulgent, something you hardly ever find in “healthy” food.

The wraps were high-protein, gluten-free, and filled with fresh, crunchy veggies — genuinely delicious without feeling heavy. The warm salad bowl was another highlight; wholesome, hearty, and full of bold flavors that don’t make you miss regular fast food at all.

And the cold coffee? Smooth, beautifully balanced, and made without any artificial syrups — sweetened naturally and done right. Love that they also offer millet milk and almond milk options for people who prefer vegan or gut-friendly alternatives.

EarthBuns isn’t just a café — it’s a whole new way of eating without compromise. Super impressed by their concept and the honesty behind their ingredients.

If you're health-conscious, gluten-intolerant, or simply want guilt-free comfort food that still tastes amazing, this place is a must-visit.
“Healthy and Tasty” isn’t just their tagline — it’s exactly what they deliver.

Can't wait to go back and try more!

Whether you are looking for gluten-free burgers in Mumbai, vegan-friendly wraps, or refined sugar-free desserts, EarthBuns has set a new benchmark. Every dish reflects their commitment to clean eating, sustainability, and big flavors. It’s not just a meal, it’s a movement for mindful indulgence.

featured_reviews.name: Prathamesh dalvi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Instagrammable Bandra café with average food and high prices 📸

Visited Juco Café around 2 PM for lunch. The café is quite small and a bit cramped with just about four tables, but I have to say — the ambience is super aesthetic, vibrant, and cozy. It’s one of those cute little spots that photograph really well and give off good vibes.

We ordered a few things to try:
🍜 Japanese Ramen Bowl (₹520) – The quantity was generous, and the flavours were quite nice. It’s a comforting bowl and filling enough for one person.
🍳 Shakshouka (₹400) – This one was surprisingly good! The taste was on point, and the portion size was enough for two people to share.
🥤 Blueberry Spirulina Smoothie (₹400) – Sadly, this was the only miss for us. It mostly tasted like banana with barely any blueberry flavour, so it didn’t feel worth the price.

The service was quite slow — it took about 35–40 minutes for our food to arrive, even though the café wasn’t crowded when we visited.

Overall, I’d give 3/5 stars. The pricing is definitely on the higher side, and while the food was decent, it’s not something I’d crave to go back for (except maybe to try their smoothie bowls next time!).
